A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same USB research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated algorithms and renumbered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original trajectory-reconstruction experiments on synthetic and biological datasets, branching simulations, and sensitivity analyses in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds division-event validation, branch-occupancy measurements, computational comparisons, approximation tests, and qualitative comparator experiments.

M1.justification: The specified score-loss weight changes from sqrt(νt(1−t)) to νsqrt(t(1−t)) in B.1. The semi-coupling algorithm changes δ from sqrt(ν/(2λ)) to ν/sqrt(λ) in B.3. These are localized formula corrections; the architecture, conditional paths, and inference algorithms remain. The PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The existing synthetic and biological datasets remain. Appendix C.11 adds one-dimensional mass splitting and two-dimensional transport between five source and five target points, with imbalance factors from 0.7 to 2.0. These extend approximation-testing scenarios without expanding biological coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D.7 adds actual qualitative evaluations of PAGA and Slingshot. New comparisons assess resources against DeepRUOT, SF2M, and WFR-FM, and WFR couplings against numerically optimized RUOT. The comparator sets in the existing accuracy tables remain unchanged; Palantir and RNA-velocity methods are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Substantial new evaluation protocols include 2,000 branching trajectories over 400 steps with 100-bin event-count evaluation, and K-means classification of 15,700 simulated trajectories for branch occupancy. Appendix C.10 adds runtime and peak-memory evaluation on one H200 with specified training settings. These supplement the retained benchmark protocols rather than replacing them.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's sensitivity analyses and qualitative branching demonstration, v2 quantitatively tests microscopic division events and macroscopic branch occupancy. It also adds direct WFR-approximation checks and PAGA/Slingshot failure case studies. These substantially extend scrutiny of the approximation and discrete-dynamics claims.

E5.justification: Existing five-run mean and standard-deviation reporting is retained. No new seed, confidence-interval, significance-testing, or run-to-run uncertainty procedure is specified. The new trajectory counts describe evaluation sample sizes.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 3–15 remain unchanged, but substantial results are added: division-count correlation 0.9950 with 10.7% relative error; predicted Dyngen branch proportions 0.650:0.350 versus 0.708:0.292; and a shared splitting optimum of 0.303 in C.11. Table 16 newly reports USB runtime of 70.10 seconds versus DeepRUOT's 2007.85 seconds at 49,302 cells under the new H200 protocol.

T1.justification: The RUOT integrand changes from one-half of the combined velocity and growth penalties to one-half of the velocity penalty plus the growth penalty. Equations 11 and 46–48 revise the conjugate and growth-penalty scaling, with corresponding changes in Appendix A.4 and the no-growth derivation in D.1. The central theorem statements remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about simulation-free stochastic unbalanced modeling and discrete birth-death simulation. The new evidence supports these existing contributions; the approximation reminder in Section 4 is consistent with v1's already stated WFR limitation.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes quadratic CPU-memory growth to OT precomputation, interprets WFR accuracy under moderate imbalance, and attributes PAGA/Slingshot errors to missing temporal information. Appendix G extends the applicability discussion to an unqualified assertion that moderate biological imbalance always holds. The original intractability limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability address, hardware and training settings for the new resource benchmark, and a SciPy implementation reference for numerical RUOT optimization. New Appendix G supplies hardware, parameter-tuning, and offspring-distribution advice. Most existing implementation details remain unchanged; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: New Appendix D.7 introduces PAGA, Slingshot, Palantir, and RNA-velocity literature, adding six cited works and distinguishing temporal-snapshot transport from inference without observed time information. Existing positioning relative to OT, Schrödinger bridges, and matching methods is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical and heading-capitalization edits, clarifies weighted-particle terminology, and updates publication information. It moves training pseudocode from Appendix F into Section 5 and adds several appendix subsections and practitioner advice. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands substantially through the event-count plot, approximation cost curves and coupling heatmaps, PAGA/Slingshot panels, and the runtime/memory table. Existing figures are retained and renumbered or repositioned, while training pseudocode moves into the main text. These are substantive display additions beyond pagination changes.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical consistency and adds useful quantitative checks of discrete simulation, approximation accuracy, and computational requirements, alongside code-access information. These strengthen support for the retained conclusions. The gain is limited by the small approximation examples and overstatements such as calling empirical validation rigorous proof and asserting that moderate biological imbalance always holds; the supplied tests do not establish those broader assurances.
